mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with rising corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days without requiring a specific threshold.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a tight labor market that typically precedes corporate profit growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE falls below 4.0%, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved corporate earnings outlook.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising INDPRO and PAYEMS fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%), a rising CPI (CPIAUCSL) indicates accelerating inflation that prompts central bank hawkishness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and CPIAUCSL rises, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction (HOUST) indicates strong housing market activity, which historically correlates with rising consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days without requiring a specific threshold.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where HOUST increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1800 thousand units for two consecutive months, it signals a robust housing market that typically precedes economic expansion and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST exceeds 1800, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in residential construction (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved corporate revenue outlook.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.0% year-over-year), a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary policy that typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL < 2.0% YoY and FEDFUNDS rises, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.
